reading.body:
North Dakota's tracked 2025 bills include two measures on robots specifically, one addressing law enforcement use of a robot and another creating a penalty for harassment and stalking committed with a robot, a narrower and more literal framing of AI adjacent technology than the deepfake, disclosure, and computer generated image bills that dominate other states' lists.

The state also directed legislative attention toward computer generated imagery through two bills, a prohibition on possessing certain computer generated images and a separate deepfake video and image prohibition, alongside a management study on criminal conduct against children, showing child protection concerns intersecting with AI generated content legislation here as in other states.

Two grant program bills, one for a research technology park and another combining a state IT research center, an advanced technology review committee, and a compute credits grant program, point to North Dakota also treating AI and advanced computing as an economic development target requiring public investment and infrastructure like compute credits, not only a subject to regulate.

The data does not indicate which of these 16 bills passed, failed, or remain pending, nor does it include bill text beyond title and number, so North Dakota's actual enacted framework covering robots, deepfakes, and AI infrastructure investment is not established by this record.
